6506 IEEE TRANSACTIONS ON DEPENDABLE AND SECURE COMPUTING, VOL. 23, NO. 3, MAY/JUNE 2026   RedAgent: An Autonomous Agent for Context-Aware Red Teaming of   LLM Jailbreaks Huiyu Xu , Wenhui Zhang, Zhibo Wang , Senior Member, IEEE, Feng Xiao, Rui Zheng ,   Zhongjie Ba , Member, IEEE, and Kui Ren , Fellow, IEEE   Abstract—Recently, Large Language Models (LLMs) have been integrated into many real-world applications like Code Copilot. These applications have significantly expanded the attack surface of LLMs, exposing them to complex real-world jailbreak threats. Despite the promising advances in actively finding jailbreak vulner- abilities of LLMs (i.e., red teaming) in general contexts, identifying these threats in complex domain-specific contexts (e.g, mathemati- cal LLMs) remains underexplored. In this paper, we study whether the context these real-world LLM applications work in, including different system prompts, tools, and scenarios of tasks, give rise to context-specific jailbreak threats. Particularly, we adapt general jailbreak prompts to the context of the target application via LLM rewriting to generate context-specific attacks. By measuring the differences in jailbreak responses between general attacks and context-specific attacks, we reveal that customized domain-specific LLMs are more vulnerable in their specific context.

By measuring the differences in jailbreak responses between general attacks and context-specific attacks, we reveal that customized domain-specific LLMs are more vulnerable in their specific context. Motivated by this observation, we propose a context-aware red teaming ap- proach, RedAgent, to generate context-specific jailbreak attacks towards customized LLM applications. Through effectively re- trieving and updating structured knowledge in an agent system, RedAgent efficiently perceive and utilize contextual information to adapt the jailbreak prompts to the target contexts. Extensive exper- iments show that our system can jailbreak most black-box LLMs within just five queries, improving the efficiency of existing red teaming methods by two times. Further, RedAgent can effectively jailbreak customized LLM applications. By generating context- specific jailbreak prompts towards 60 trending applications on the marketplace of OpenAI, we discover 600 vulnerabilities of these real-world applications with only two queries per vulnerability. Typical red teams explore potential jailbreak variants randomly, often relying on general templates derived from past trials and thus lacking contextual relevance. Since existing methods do not explicitly estimate or leverage contex- tual information from target LLM responses, they fail to adapt prompts to specific contexts effectively. iii) Diversity of prompt refinement: Typical red teaming approaches are limited to using a few mutation operations to refine jailbreak templates. This restricted action space limits the automation of adaptive prompt generation, often leading to ineffective refinement. The key requirement for context-specific red-teaming is to dynamically adapt attacks based on contextual information estimated from responses, which demands a more diverse and flexible action space that existing methods do not provide.   To address these challenges, we propose RedAgent, a novel red teaming method that automatically perceives the context and adjusts the general jailbreak prompts into context-specific ones based on it. To enable scalability and flexibility in red team knowledge, we propose modeling existing jailbreak prompts as structured representations of jailbreak strategies. These strate- gies, organized into structured text, act as flexible conditions for generating adaptive prompts that can be applied across varying contexts. Upon such modeling, we enhance the contextual rel- evance of generated prompts via building a context-aware red team. Unlike previous methods, we optimize the red teaming knowledge at two levels: the global strategy level (i.e., long-term memory) and the contextual modification level (i.e., short-term memory).

Each LLM is prompted by specific instructions to perform different roles. Here is the pipeline of RedAgent:   i) Red Team Knowledge Construction: The summarizer LLM abstracts collected jailbreak prompts into strategies as the ini- tialization of the long-term memory.   ii) Context-guided Jailbreak Prompt Generation: Given an initial jailbreak goal, the retrieval LLM searches relevant strate- gies from long-term memory.
